about: Generalisation design G18 (train), in dev.json format. Tier 4 = a mechanical part with bought-in fasteners and a bearing: a two-piece split pillow block, a press/clamp fit judged on the closed bore, captive nuts, and a mounting pattern. L1 ids match requirements.md next to this file. Numbers that are not in the request words come from requirements.md and are provisional until the owner confirms them. Never put any of these numbers in agent logic: they belong in the request text and in generalize/parts/*/part.json.

methods.inspection: read from the design or mesh (counts, sizes, positions, relations)
methods.analysis: computed by Python (stability, connectivity, interference and clearance against reference models, hand calculations)
methods.demonstration: a stand-in object is placed in the design (fits, rests, does not slide)
methods.test: a probe is applied (insert a plug along its axis, drop the board in, load path, slide the drawer)

requests.title: 608 bearing split pillow block
requests.request: A two-piece pillow block for a 608 bearing (8 x 22 x 7 mm) that is clamped, not glued. The block is split along the bearing axis into a base and a cap. Two M3 bolts with captive hex nuts pull the halves together, and the bearing pocket is about 0.1 mm under 22 mm across when the halves are closed, so the clamp holds the bearing. The base has two M4 mounting holes 40 mm apart. It is printed on an FDM printer without supports.
requests.request_verbatim: A two-piece pillow block for a 608 bearing (8 x 22 x 7 mm) that is clamped, not glued. Two M3 bolts with captive hex nuts pull the halves together, and the bearing bore pocket should be about 0.1 mm under 22 mm so the clamp holds it. The base has two M4 mounting holes 40 mm apart.
requests.request_notes: Added to the plan brief, from requirements.md section 3: the split plane contains the bearing axis, base below, cap above (D1); pocket diameter 21.9 measured with the halves closed (D2); the M4 holes are 40 mm apart along the bearing axis (D3); the nuts sit in hex pockets in the base open to the split face (D4); FDM, no supports (A8).

l1.text: The block shall be two separate printed bodies, a base and a cap, split along a plane that contains the bearing axis, and closed they shall meet on that plane.
With the halves closed, the bearing pocket shall be 21.9 mm across (21.85 to 21.95 mm), round, and centred on the bearing axis, so that the 22 mm bearing is squeezed by about 0.1 mm.
The pocket shall hold the 7 mm wide bearing axially between two lips on the outer ring, and nothing printed shall touch the bearing's inner ring or bore.
The closed halves shall touch on the split plane (gap at most 0.05 mm) over a real area (at least 100 mm2), so the bolts clamp the halves onto the bearing and not onto each other's gap.
Two M3 bolts, one on each side of the bearing, shall pass through clearance holes in the cap, with their heads counterbored, into the base.
Each bolt shall thread into an M3 hex nut held captive in a hex pocket in the base, open to the split face, so the nut cannot fall out or turn once the cap is on.
The base shall have two M4 mounting holes 40.0 mm apart with room for the heads and a hex key.
With the cap off, the bearing shall drop into the base half and the nuts into their pockets; with the cap on, every bolt and mounting screw shall be reachable with a hex key.

The load shall reach the mounting holes through solid material: at least 2.5 mm of wall between the bearing pocket and any outer surface, at least 2.0 mm round every hole, counterbore and nut pocket, at least 100 mm2 of base cross-section on every plane between the block and each M4 hole, and no more than 10 MPa bending stress in the base for a 100 N pull on the bearing; the base shall be one connected body.
The base and the cap shall each be one manifold body that prints on an FDM printer without supports in its stated print orientation.
The closed block shall be no larger than 60 x 60 x 32 mm and shall stand flat on its mounting face without tipping.

The design shall be delivered as a base STL, a cap STL (closed assembly pose, mm), the OpenSCAD source, the declared hardware layout and the agent's own measurement report, and that report shall agree with an independent measurement.

beyond_library: split body: one pocket shape cut across two bodies on the split plane, closed pose with a stated gap
press/clamp fit: pocket diameter derived from the bearing's outer diameter and a stated interference, measured on the closed bore
captive hex nut pocket (true hexagon from the nut's across-flats) open to a face, plus counterbore for the bolt head
bolt pattern: two bolt axes symmetric about the bearing, two mounting holes at a stated pitch
bearing lips and free-bore rule from the catalogue part
load path: wall and ligament thickness checks, bending of the plate section
